title: Artificial intelligence adoption in technical-vocational higher education: employability and workforce policy implications
text_snippet: Artificial intelligence adoption in technical-vocational higher education: employability and workforce policy implications Purpose This study investigated students' experiences of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in Technical-Vocational Higher Education (TVHE) in Jolo, Sulu, Philippines, examining its implications for learning, employability, and institutional readiness. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative phenomenological design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with fifteen purposively selected TVHE students. Data were analyzed through Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis, interpreted using the Technology Acceptance Model, Human Capital Theory, and Digital Governance Theory. Findings Students perceived AI as a continuously available learning scaffold that supported academic learning, practical-skills preparation, and employability readiness, while expressing concerns about information reliability and over-reliance. Effective AI adoption was perceived to require institutional readiness, including infrastructure, AI-literacy training, and ethical governance. title: Responsible and sustainable use of AIGC image tools in art education: an SEM–ANN–fsQCA study
text_snippet: Responsible and sustainable use of AIGC image tools in art education: an SEM–ANN–fsQCA study Purpose This study examines how responsible and sustainable use intention (RSU) toward artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) image tools is formed in higher education art and design classrooms. Existing research has mainly explained generative AI use through technology acceptance or continuance logic, while paying limited attention to the aesthetic, authenticity-related and classroom-governance conditions under which long-term use becomes norm-compliant and educationally sustainable. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the stimuli, organismic states and response (S–O–R) framework, this study models perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and perceived classroom digital fairness as stimuli; digital aesthetic fatigue, authenticity–authorship anxiety and perceived authenticity of AIGC images as organismic states; and RSU as the response. GenAI literacy is included as a moderator. Data from 1,238 higher education art and design students were analysed using PLS-SEM, ANN and fsQCA. title: Integrating user behaviour into sustainable urban transformation: machine learning model from university campus
text_snippet: Integrating user behaviour into sustainable urban transformation: machine learning model from university campus Purpose This research proposes a data-driven model situated at the intersection of occupancy, sustainable design and building utilisation. The model is designed to assess the sustainability performance of the existing campus building stock while offering predictive insights for future developments. A university campus was selected as a controlled “micro-city” environment to address the difficulties of collecting consistent city-scale data. The main objective is to demonstrate how occupancy, operational and spatial information can be integrated through machine learning (ML) to support a gradual and human-centred urban transformation process. Design/methodology/approach An open-access Green Campus Dataset comprising 2,138 data points representing environmental, spatial and socioeconomic variables was analysed. Following exploratory correlation analysis and feature engineering, seven ML algorithms – linear regression, random forest, gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron (MLP), K-nearest neighbours (KNN), support vector regression (SVR) and XGBoost – were comparatively evaluated for predicting energy savings. title: Student engagement in “becoming employable”: a comparative case study of master’s students from two universities in China
text_snippet: Student engagement in “becoming employable”: a comparative case study of master’s students from two universities in China Purpose This study explores how master’s students in China engage in employability building, examining the influence of family socioeconomic status (SES) and institutional type on their cognitive, affective and behavioral engagement dimensions. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comparative case study design, the research draws on semi-structured interviews with 37 master’s students from two distinct university contexts in China: a local public university (S University) and a Sino-British cooperative university (X University). Data were analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings Students’ engagement in employability building manifests across cognitive (labor market intelligence, self-awareness, reflective career planning), affective (career identity, stress management, emotional resilience) and behavioral (career exploration, skill development, networking) dimensions. title: Understanding generation Z’s credulity toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI): a qualitative study
text_snippet: Understanding generation Z’s credulity toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI): a qualitative study Purpose The aim of this paper is to investigate the cognitive and motivational factors underlying the credulity of Generation Z users toward generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and to trace the consequences of this phenomenon. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory qualitative study was conducted in 2024 involving 36 Vietnamese Generation Z participants (26 in-depth interview participants and 10 focus group participants) who had used GenAI tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini. Data were collected through semi-structured in-depth interviews and focus group interviews and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase thematic analysis framework to explore the cognitive and motivational factors underlying Generation Z’s credulity toward GenAI. Findings The present study revealed that Generation Z users' over-reliance on GenAI is largely motivated by habitual trust, cognitive offloading and emphasis on efficiency rather than accuracy. text_snippet: Teaching beyond technology: student ratings of TPACK-informed teaching in a Sino-British transnational entrepreneurship programme Purpose Technology plays an increasingly important role in entrepreneurship education, particularly within transnational higher education where culturally diverse classrooms require effective alignment of disciplinary content, pedagogy, and digital technologies. Despite the growing use of the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, limited research has examined students' evaluations of TPACK-informed teaching in entrepreneurship education. This study investigates undergraduate students' perceptions within a Sino-British transnational entrepreneurship programme. text_snippet: Bridging perception gaps: a comparative analysis of student interns' self-evaluations versus mentors' evaluations across technical and soft skills Purpose This study aims to examine how the alignment between interns' self-evaluations and mentors' assessments across technical and soft or professional skills influences overall internship success in a work integrated learning (WIL) context. It also explores whether miscalibration, that is, the overestimation or underestimation of competence, affects performance evaluations and overall employability outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Paired survey data were collected from 290 undergraduate interns and their workplace mentors in business-related programs at a Saudi university. Using exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses followed by partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM), the study tested a multi-domain model linking self-ratings, mentor evaluations, perception gaps, and overall success. title: Exploring factors affecting Chinese students studying abroad: social media analytics during and after COVID-19
text_snippet: Exploring factors affecting Chinese students studying abroad: social media analytics during and after COVID-19 Purpose This study examines how the sentiments and perceptions of Chinese students studying abroad evolved during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Drawing on social media data, the study identifies key factors related to educational choice, vocational preparation and transitions into employment. Design/methodology/approach This study analyzed nearly 95,000 Weibo posts related to studying abroad and COVID-19. Computational data mining methods, including sentiment analysis and topic modeling, were employed to identify key themes and emotional patterns among Chinese students considering studying abroad. The Granger causality test was utilized to explore the relationships between COVID-19 case numbers and sentiment scores. Findings Results revealed that policy factors, health considerations and future development concerns related to degree recognition, graduate employability, salary expectations, job stability and career competitiveness are critical issues affecting Chinese students’ decisions to study abroad. title: Letting go of ghost ships and the longitudinal development of opportunity-cost fear among students in entrepreneurial teams
text_snippet: Letting go of ghost ships and the longitudinal development of opportunity-cost fear among students in entrepreneurial teams Purpose A longitudinal account of opportunity-cost fear in entrepreneurship education is developed and tested. Opportunity-cost fear is anxiety that venture participation displaces other valued activities, life events and relationships. The study asks whether students’ perceptions of alignment and conflict within educational venture teams are associated with this fear as projects unfold. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on appraisal theory, entrepreneurial emotion and new venture team research, the study analyses three matched survey waves from 74 entrepreneurship students. The unit of analysis is the individual student, with alignment, conflict and quality treated as perceptions of the student’s venture team. title: From hindsight to employability insight: graduate experiences of a developmental assessment centre
text_snippet: From hindsight to employability insight: graduate experiences of a developmental assessment centre Purpose This study extends prior research by examining graduate perceptions of how a developmental assessment centre (DAC) and associated work-integrated learning (WIL) placements contribute to graduate employability (GE) as defined by Caballero et al.’s (2026) capability framework. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods survey with optional interviews was conducted with postgraduate psychology graduates at least six months post-graduation. Participants reflected on the DAC’s contributions and suggested improvements. Findings Graduates confirmed that the DAC had a sustained positive impact on their GE development and promoted early emphasis on personal and professional development aligned with workplace expectations. title: AI literacy and AI-supported chatbot adoption for educators’ professional performance
text_snippet: AI literacy and AI-supported chatbot adoption for educators’ professional performance Purpose As artificial intelligence (AI)–supported chatbots are increasingly deployed in higher education worldwide, identifying the factors that shape educators’ adoption of these tools for professional performance has become a globally relevant issue. This study investigates the key factors influencing educators’ adoption of AI-supported chatbots, with a particular focus on their perceived impact on professional performance. Design/methodology/approach We analyzed two-wave survey data collected from 535 educators employed at Chinese higher vocational and professional tertiary education to examine the relationships among key determinants, educators’ attitudes and intentions, and their adoption behavior of AI-supported chatbots for performance. Findings The results reveal that perceived usefulness, effort expectancy, AI literacy and social influence significantly affect educators’ attitudes and intentions, which in turn predict the adoption behavior of AI-supported chatbots for performance. title: Eco-anxiety among university students: institutional support, sustainable action and psychological resilience
text_snippet: Eco-anxiety among university students: institutional support, sustainable action and psychological resilience Purpose Eco-anxiety (EA) is now a prevalent form of climate-related distress among university students, yet most evidence has been generated in the Global North. Drawing on the self-determination theory (SDT) and conservation of resources (COR) theory, we examine how perceived institutional support relates to EA in a climate-vulnerable Global South setting. We test whether engagement in sustainable lifestyle practices mediates this relationship and whether psychological resilience moderates the link between sustainable practices and EA. Design/methodology/approach We surveyed a total of 539 students enrolled in public and private universities in Bangladesh and tested the model using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings Perceived institutional support is associated with lower EA. title: “All that remains is a diploma”: employability, policy-induced mismatch and school-to-work transitions in health vocational education
text_snippet: “All that remains is a diploma”: employability, policy-induced mismatch and school-to-work transitions in health vocational education Purpose This study examines how students in health vocational high schools (HVHS) in Türkiye perceive their employability, anticipated school-to-work transitions and developing professional identities within the post-2014 qualification structure. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on career construction theory and policy feedback theory, the study adopts a qualitative case study design based on semi-structured interviews with students across two HVHS. Findings The findings reveal an education–employment mismatch manifested in four interrelated patterns: externally driven school choice, inherited expectations and post-reform disappointment, perceived misalignment between vocational training and post-graduation opportunities, and the psychosocial cost of policy change. Practical implications The findings contribute to international debates on vocationalism, youth employability and school-to-work transitions by highlighting the psychosocial and identity-related consequences of policy-induced educational mismatch. title: Selective adoption of AI in entrepreneurship education: a micro-narrative analysis of student rejection and ambivalence
text_snippet: Selective adoption of AI in entrepreneurship education: a micro-narrative analysis of student rejection and ambivalence Purpose This study aims to examine how university entrepreneurship students make sense of artificial intelligence (AI) in their courses, focusing on narratives of rejection and ambivalence rather than simple adoption, aiming to inform pedagogical approaches that are both effective and ethically grounded. Design/methodology/approach We analysed 606 anonymous micro-narratives from entrepreneurship students at two Catalan universities. title: Preparing students for entrepreneurial careers: the contributions of experiential pedagogies
text_snippet: Preparing students for entrepreneurial careers: the contributions of experiential pedagogies Purpose This study aims to examine the effects of entrepreneurship education on entrepreneurial self-efficacy, entrepreneurial identity, and career crystallization. Design/methodology/approach A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was adopted. title: The motivation model and characteristics of Chinese college students' entrepreneurship: an empirical study based on grounded theory
text_snippet: The motivation model and characteristics of Chinese college students' entrepreneurship: an empirical study based on grounded theory Purpose This paper aims to explore the formation mechanism of entrepreneurial motivation among Chinese college students and its influence on entrepreneurial behaviors. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts purposive sampling and conducts in-depth semi-structured interviews with 21 outstanding college student entrepreneurs. Guided by classic grounded theory, this research carries out three rounds of coding procedures including open coding, axial coding and selective coding. Theoretical saturation test is further implemented to verify the robustness of the constructed model. Findings The results reveal that college students’ entrepreneurial motivation is a compound driving system shaped by the interplay of internal and external factors, which consists of three core dimensions: spiritual drive, material drive and external drive. Although individual traits and practical experiences do not serve as direct motivational factors, they act as fundamental preconditions. title: Paving the way: an exploration of sustainable career development for teachers in China's vocational colleges
text_snippet: Paving the way: an exploration of sustainable career development for teachers in China's vocational colleges Purpose Vocational college teachers are facing policy volatility, intensified performance management, and complex cross-boundary expectations. These pressures threaten long-term career sustainability. However, existing research focuses primarily on compulsory and higher education, leaving vocational teachers largely overlooked. To address this gap, this study employs career ecosystem theory (CET) to investigate how Chinese vocational college teachers sustain their careers within a policy-driven environment involving multiple stakeholders. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an exploratory qualitative design. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 24 vocational college teachers across seven Chinese provinces. Data were analysed inductively and interpretively through the lens of CET to map ecosystem-level constraints and teachers’ adaptive responses. title: Modeling career decision competency for global vocational education: confirmatory factor analysis evidence from Thailand with cross-cultural implications
text_snippet: Modeling career decision competency for global vocational education: confirmatory factor analysis evidence from Thailand with cross-cultural implications Purpose This study reframes career decision-making competency in vocational education as a system-embedded capability influenced by institutional supports, opportunity structures, and constraints. text_snippet: The architecture of AI credentials: how design quality and educational context build self-efficacy and shape readiness for AI-intensive work Purpose This study examines how the design of AI-focused higher education credentials shapes students' readiness for AI-intensive work. text_snippet: Pathways to self-employed reemployment: motivations and learning strategies among late baby boomers Purpose This study explored the motivations and learning strategies through which older adults from the late baby boomer cohort in Taiwan pursue reemployment through self-employment. text_snippet: Artificial intelligence and marketing education: mapping current research and emerging patterns Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping marketing education and to assess the extent to which marketing education addresses technological transformation within education contexts. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a systematic bibliometric review to examine the intersection of AI and marketing education. title: Bridging university and family support: a moderated mediation model of career adapting responses
text_snippet: Bridging university and family support: a moderated mediation model of career adapting responses Purpose Drawing on career construction theory (CCT) and sustainable career ecosystem theory (SCET), this study examines when and under what relational conditions university support translates into students' career adapting responses. title: Developing oral communication skills and self-regulation through social media-based mobile microlearning: a CareerEDGE model perspective
text_snippet: Developing oral communication skills and self-regulation through social media-based mobile microlearning: a CareerEDGE model perspective Purpose This study evaluates how a social media-based mobile microlearning (SMBMM) intervention via WeChat fosters undergraduate oral communication skills and self-regulation, positioning them within the CareerEDGE model. title: Effective delivery of degree apprenticeships (DA) in the built environment: the role of infrastructure in higher education institutions (HEI) and workplace
text_snippet: Effective delivery of degree apprenticeships (DA) in the built environment: the role of infrastructure in higher education institutions (HEI) and workplace Purpose The aim of this paper is to explore the current infrastructure provided to degree apprenticeships (DA) students by higher education institutions (HEIs) and workplace to enhance the effective delivery of DA in the built environment (BE). Design/methodology/approach The research employed a mixed-methods approach gathering both qualitative and quantitative data through a questionnaire that captured the perceptions of 57 apprentices from a UK university who were completing a DA related to the BE. Findings Whilst the majority of the apprentices were satisfied with the infrastructure provided by the HEI, they suggested that the work-based module, effective communication, time-tabling and assessment deadlines could be improved. The apprentices appreciated support from their workplaces, including that provided by mentors and colleagues, especially with regard to well-being services and practical opportunities such as site visits. title: Sectoral training matters more than improvement in foundation skills: how Australian VET programs are associated with graduate employability
text_snippet: Sectoral training matters more than improvement in foundation skills: how Australian VET programs are associated with graduate employability Purpose This study questions whether foundational skills are associated with occupational mobility in Australian VET for those employed prior to taking up VET training, or if sectoral context matters more. We test whether gains in numeracy/literacy/problem solving skills outweigh training package type as the strongest predictor of career advancement. Design/methodology/approach We analyze 2023 NCVER survey data (n = 64,873) of employed VET completers who were also employed prior to their training, calculating occupational status gain using McMillan's ANZCO-based scale. Regression and dominance analysis assess impacts of skill improvements, training package, qualification level, age and gender. Findings Average gain was 2.7 points. Self-reported writing improvement showed modest benefit; self-reported numeracy gains correlated with lower status; self-reported problem-solving had weak effect. ICT and Aeroskills delivered highest gains; Furnishing and Transport and Logistics showed negative outcomes. Younger graduates (20–24 yrs) gained nearly double older cohorts. title: Stepping into the future: how robotic simulation training equips hospitality graduates for automated workplaces
text_snippet: Stepping into the future: how robotic simulation training equips hospitality graduates for automated workplaces Purpose This study examines the effectiveness of robotic simulation training (RST) in improving hospitality graduates' employability through soft and hard technological skill acquisition in automated workplaces. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 548 hospitality technology graduates in the Middle Eastern and North African countries. A partial least squares structural equation model was used to analyze the data. Findings The results showed that RST positively affected the acquisition of both soft and hard technological skills. Such abilities increased the perceived likelihood of labor market entry. The findings indicate that technological skill acquisition represents the primary explanatory pathway through which RST enhances graduates' perceived employability. Nevertheless, industry demand for technological skills does not moderate these relationships. title: The engagement–capability gap in higher education: evidence from UK and Türkiye students
text_snippet: The engagement–capability gap in higher education: evidence from UK and Türkiye students Purpose This study examines students’ self-reported digital and soft skills, together with learning-related communication practices in higher education, and explores whether these profiles differ by programme and year of study in the United Kingdom and Türkiye. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from the United Kingdom (N = 85) and Türkiye (N = 122). Items captured learning resource use, communication practices, digital skills (DigComp 2.2-aligned) and soft skills on 5-point Likert scales. Differences across domains were examined using Friedman tests (Kendall’s W). Associations were examined using Spearman correlations with 95% confidence intervals. Item-level group differences by programme/year were tested using the Kruskal–Wallis test with BH–FDR correction; significant items were followed by Dunn post-hoc tests (BH–FDR). title: Extracurricular work experiences and soft skills development among pre-service teachers
text_snippet: Extracurricular work experiences and soft skills development among pre-service teachers Purpose This study explores how extracurricular work experiences relate to the development of soft skills among pre-service teachers. Soft skills such as social competences, communication, flexibility, efficacy beliefs and lifelong learning are crucial for addressing complex classroom challenges and supporting professional growth, yet whether work experiences may help foster them remains underexplored. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed with 709 pre-service teachers enrolled in two bachelor’s programmes in educational sciences. Data was gathered through an online questionnaire at the start of the 2024–2025 academic year. Findings Results indicate that extracurricular work experiences are positively associated with social competencies and communication skills, but show no significant effect on efficacy beliefs or flexibility. Interestingly, pre-service teachers with work experience reported lower lifelong learning skills. Originality/value This study contributes to the limited research on how extracurricular work shapes soft skill acquisition in teacher education. title: Educational robotics in technical and vocational education and training: a technology surveillance-based strategic roadmap
text_snippet: Educational robotics in technical and vocational education and training: a technology surveillance-based strategic roadmap Purpose This study develops a strategic roadmap for educational robotics in Colombia's Technical and Vocational Education and Training system. It examines how robotics education can anticipate technological, occupational and institutional changes linked to Industry 4.0. Design/methodology/approach The study combines technology surveillance with participatory roadmapping. Bibliometric mapping of Scopus publications and expert focus groups were used to identify technological drivers, emerging roles, research, development and innovation lines and capabilities across short-, medium- and long-term horizons. Findings Five drivers emerged: mobile robots, human–robot interaction, industrial robotics, self-reconfigurable modular robots and soft robotics. Emerging roles were linked to robotics operation, programming, interface development, engineering and team coordination. Nine research, development and innovation lines were prioritised, with gaps in human talent, infrastructure and alliances. Research limitations/implications Findings depend on expert judgement and a Colombian case. Broader participation would improve transferability. title: Artificial intelligence drivers for business education: a systematic review using the ADO framework
text_snippet: Artificial intelligence drivers for business education: a systematic review using the ADO framework Purpose This systematic literature review (SLR) aims to comprehensively examine previously published articles on the drivers of artificial intelligence (AI) to identify the key drivers and develop a future agenda for AI in business education. Design/methodology/approach In this study, using The Population, Intervention, Comparison, and Outcome (PICO) and Preferred Reporting Items For Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocols, we selected 35 published articles, and the researchers employed antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) framework was employed for the final synthesis. Findings The 19 most relevant AI drivers were identified for business education. However, five of those (technology selection for the classroom, technical support for teachers and students, common student-teacher perceptions of AI, students’ and teacher's prior experience of using AI, the teachers’ and students’ non-technical AI-related skills) were identified as antecedents. title: An exploratory methodological pilot of Likert Scale for Dual Identities as a reflective elicitation tool in further education identity research
text_snippet: An exploratory methodological pilot of Likert Scale for Dual Identities as a reflective elicitation tool in further education identity research Purpose This paper explores the intersection between workforce development and dual professionalism in the UK further education (FE) sector, foregrounding teacher identity as a site of both conflict and transformation. It addresses the under-theorisation of FE practitioners' dual roles, as subject specialists and pedagogues, particularly in the context of recent policy imperatives such as the Skills for Jobs White Paper and the Labour Party’s national missions. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative methodology that utilises semi-structured interviews situated in vocational teaching contexts. Drawing on data from a practitioner-led research project, it introduces a new conceptual and practical tool, the Likert Scales for Dual Identities, to map the evolution of FE educator identity. The research investigates how educators negotiate the competing demands of industry relevance and pedagogical excellence. Findings The study provides evidence of ongoing reflective practice and identity transformation among FE practitioners. title: Entrepreneurship education and graduate work-readiness: an employability-focused training perspective in higher education
text_snippet: Entrepreneurship education and graduate work-readiness: an employability-focused training perspective in higher education Purpose This study examines entrepreneurship education (EE) as a structured, employability-focused training mechanism in higher education. It aims to empirically test how EE pedagogies develop transferable competencies and enhance graduate work-readiness, addressing the disconnect between EE and employability scholarship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed. The quantitative phase involved a survey of 412 final-year students and recent graduates, with data analyzed via structural equation modelling. The qualitative phase comprised 24 in-depth interviews, analyzed thematically to contextualize the quantitative pathways. Findings Entrepreneurship education pedagogies (EEP) strongly predict employability competencies (EC) (ß = 0.632), which in turn strongly predict graduate work-readiness (GWR) (ß = 0.683). EC partially mediates the EEP-GWR relationship (ß = 0.432). title: Value-driven employability: How work values and ethics shape Generation Z's career preferences
text_snippet: Value-driven employability: How work values and ethics shape Generation Z's career preferences Purpose This study examines how Generation Z's work values and ethics differ by gender, academic discipline, and prior work experience, and how these integrated value–ethic profiles shape early-career preferences. The aim is to support universities in improving person–organisation fit and designing value-informed career-guidance interventions that foster smoother and more sustainable school-to-work transitions. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of 721 undergraduates combined two validated instruments – the Portrait Values Questionnaire (PVQ-40) and the Multidimensional Work Ethic Profile (MWEP) – with a ranking of ten job-selection factors. Group comparisons and effect-size analyses were conducted across gender, discipline, and work-experience bands. Findings Significant subgroup differences emerged in both values and ethical orientations. Across all groups, career progression and effective management consistently ranked as the top job selection priorities, while compensation and organizational culture were less emphasized. title: Learning to work: University internships and the transition to employment in Spain
text_snippet: Learning to work: University internships and the transition to employment in Spain Purpose This study examines the relationship between curricular university internships and labour market outcomes for university graduates in Spain. It investigates both short- and long-term associations across two graduate cohorts. Design/methodology/approach The analysis draws on microdata from two cohorts (2014 and 2010) of the Spanish University Graduate Job Placement Survey. Linear probability models are estimated to assess the relationship between internship participation and several labour market outcomes, including job-search duration after graduation, as well as employment and salary status five years later. To address selection and omitted variable bias, the study applies several propensity-score-based approaches and Oster's (2019) method. Findings Participation in curricular internships is consistently associated with a shorter time to secure the first job after graduation. title: Soft skills and employability in SMEs: an employer's perspective on organizational fit and university reputation
text_snippet: Soft skills and employability in SMEs: an employer's perspective on organizational fit and university reputation Purpose This study investigates how soft skills shape the employability of fresh graduates in the context of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Drawing on stakeholder theory and signaling theory, this study sets out to investigate the role of soft skills in the employability of fresh graduates, emphasizing the mediating role of organizational fit (OF) and the moderating role of university reputation. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was applied. Qualitative interviews with SME employers first identified priority soft skills and guided the survey design. Quantitative data from 167 firms were then analyzed to test the hypothesized relationships. Findings The results indicate that soft skills (SK) do not directly affect employability (EMP); instead, they exert a strong indirect influence through OF. Moreover, the moderating role of university reputation (RE) offers a more nuanced, realistic understanding of how employers evaluate both institutional credibility and individual capabilities. title: Redesigning learning pathways: recognizing non-formal competencies through micro-credentials in higher education
text_snippet: Redesigning learning pathways: recognizing non-formal competencies through micro-credentials in higher education Purpose This paper explores how micro-credentials can redefine learning pathways in higher education by recognizing competencies acquired through non-formal learning, specifically extracurricular activities. The expected contribution is twofold: (1) to provide empirical insight into the value perception of micro-credentials in the context of non-formal learning and (2) to outline design recommendations for an interoperable micro-credential ecosystem in higher education. Design/methodology/approach The study examines the perceived value and adoption of micro-credentials among key stakeholders – students as earners and employers as verifiers – focussing on factors such as perceived benefits, sacrifices, trust, and their influence on adoption intention. Guided by the Value-Based Adoption Model (VAM), parallel surveys were administered to 500 students and 63 employers. Findings The findings reveal that, for students, perceived benefits and trust are the strongest predictors of perceived value, directly shaping their intention to adopt micro-credentials. title: The kind of curriculum we need to develop integrated skills in technical and vocational training
text_snippet: The kind of curriculum we need to develop integrated skills in technical and vocational training Purpose Technical and vocational education and training (TVET) plays a critical role in preparing learners for participation in the labor market by integrating practical skills with professional competencies. This study aimed to explore experts' experiences in technical and vocational curriculum development in order to design a holistic curriculum model for formal technical and vocational education. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative research design was employed using in-depth semi-structured interviews with ten curriculum specialists and technical and vocational education experts in Iran. Participants were selected through purposive snowball sampling. Data were analyzed through systematic coding to identify key curriculum dimensions and components. Findings The findings led to the design of a holistic curriculum model grounded in a task-based approach, in which learning tasks function as the central organizing element of instruction. title: Lived experiences of science education: a preliminary exploration of students' experiences in virtual and traditional science laboratories in further education
text_snippet: Lived experiences of science education: a preliminary exploration of students' experiences in virtual and traditional science laboratories in further education Purpose This study investigates students' perspectives of the quality of their experiences learning in both traditional and virtual laboratories (VL); this is important as many settings are moving toward an expanded digital delivery. Design/methodology/approach This paper describes part of a small-scale study of level 3 science students in a large Further Education college. Questionnaires and semi-structured interviews of students and staff were used to investigate learning in both traditional and VL. A thematic analysis was carried out, gaining insights into users' views and experiences. Findings Differences in experience between traditional and VL were identified through themes of reality, control, skills, theory, truth and risk. The paper focuses on students' experience, in terms of presence and agency (related to reality and control): these two parameters can be expressed using a matrix representation, providing an analytical tool for comparing experience in traditional and VL. title: Infusing authenticity into a service-learning program: examining long-term impacts on professional development
text_snippet: Infusing authenticity into a service-learning program: examining long-term impacts on professional development Purpose The employability of postgraduate students remains a critical concern in higher education, as postgraduate programs, particularly at the doctoral level, traditionally focus on disciplinary and research competencies. This leads to a lack of adequate preparation for employment, especially for non-academic roles. This study examines the long-term impacts of an authentic service-learning program on trainees' professional lives, with a particular emphasis on academia. This addresses the need for insight into the long-term impacts of initiatives that enhance postgraduate programs with opportunities for students to acquire transferable competencies prior to entering employment. Design/methodology/approach We adopted a narrative inquiry approach to investigate the impacts of a sustained, authentic-learning-based outreach program (GK-12). To explore trainees' experiences, we used a qualitative questionnaire followed by in-depth narrative interviews. title: Strategic industry partnerships drive reform in vocational curriculum development
text_snippet: Strategic industry partnerships drive reform in vocational curriculum development Purpose This study examines how the strategic industry–institution partnerships influence vocational curriculum reform and graduate outcomes. It explores the mechanisms through which sustained collaboration enhances curriculum relevance, institutional responsiveness and alignment with evolving labour-market demands across different industry sectors. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods design was employed, combining survey data from 25 vocational institutions with semi-structured interviews involving institutional leaders and industry partners across three sectors: advanced manufacturing, healthcare services and digital technologies. Quantitative analysis assessed patterns of collaboration intensity and curriculum adaptation, while qualitative insights were used to interpret institutional and sectoral dynamics shaping partnership effectiveness. title: Institutionalizing entrepreneurship education in CDIO-based project courses: evidence from a fifteen-year longitudinal case
text_snippet: Institutionalizing entrepreneurship education in CDIO-based project courses: evidence from a fifteen-year longitudinal case Purpose This study examines how entrepreneurship education can be sustainably integrated into engineering programmes by analysing a fifteen-year case of a mandatory entrepreneurship component embedded in CDIO-based project courses at a Swedish university. It addresses the challenge that many entrepreneurship initiatives in engineering remain elective or poorly connected to technical studies. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative single case research design is used, combined with reflexive autoethnography. The analysis is triangulated with student evaluations, project materials, and programme documents from 2009 to 2025, covering more than three thousand students. The study traces the evolution of the component from early planning templates to a concise idea instrument focusing on need, user value, assumptions, uncertainties and short-term direction. title: Educating on social and sustainable enterprise, one design student at a time
text_snippet: Educating on social and sustainable enterprise, one design student at a time Purpose Design students are more than ever facing sustainability issues in their education and training, and some of them are bringing particularly relevant and timely issues to the table through their curricular projects. However, these projects often fall into oblivion after graduation and are never given a chance to be concretised. While general entrepreneurial intentions and motivations have been extensively studied, this study aims explicitly to understand and assess design students' social and sustainable entrepreneurial mindsets, intentions, and motivations, particularly those influenced by higher education and the Programme for LASALLE Creative Entrepreneurs (PLACE). Additionally, this study seeks to identify and discuss the educational implications of embedding social and sustainable entrepreneurship within design higher education programmes, offering actionable recommendations for educators and institutions aiming to foster entrepreneurial mindsets aligned with social and environmental responsibility. title: How to evaluate online learning resources for vocational education? An evaluation scale development in China
text_snippet: How to evaluate online learning resources for vocational education? An evaluation scale development in China Purpose This research aims to construct an evaluation scale of Online Learning Resource for Vocational Education (OLRVE) tailored to assess the vocational online learning resource from the perspectives of vocational students. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the ecological framework of technology uses in school, evaluative items have been established with empirical testing, which was conducted with 1,912 respondents, incorporating item refinement, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, measurement invariance testing and reliability assessments. Findings A three-dimensional evaluation tool called the OLRVE, consisting of the “educational design evaluation” (EDE), “technological design evaluation” (TDE) and “education-technological interaction evaluation” (ETIE) with ten items, has been created. text_snippet: Uncertainty by design: pedagogical approaches for learning to navigate uncertainty in entrepreneurship education Purpose This study explores how educators design learning experiences to help students manage uncertainty in entrepreneurship education. Design/methodology/approach This study uses semi-structured interviews with experienced entrepreneurship educators. The interviews were transcribed and analyzed using thematic analysis. Findings The study identifies the teaching approaches and resources utilized by educators, along with associated challenges. text_snippet: How self-directed experiential learning shapes the development of entrepreneurship competences: insights from reflective practice in an internship context Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore the development of entrepreneurship competences (EC) shaped by self-directed experiential learning (SDEL) within business and entrepreneurship studies internships. Design/methodology/approach The investigation applied deductive qualitative research guided by SDEL framework. Students' weekly reflections on entrepreneurship internships were analyzed to identify enabling and constraining behavior, affecting EC development. Seventeen undergraduate students provided their written consent to the use of their reflections for this study. Lists of keywords were then inductively derived from the coded data to characterize empirically confirmed SDEL patterns. Keyword distribution was analyzed throughout the reflections on EntreComp-defined competences. Findings The study identified distinct patterns through which self-directed learning (SDL) would either enable or limit the progression across Kolb's experiential learning (EL) phases in the development of EC. title: Early career trajectories of vocational high school graduates: the roles of educational and career readiness
text_snippet: Early career trajectories of vocational high school graduates: the roles of educational and career readiness Purpose This study examines the early career trajectories of vocational high school graduates and identifies the factors shaping their transition from school to the workforce. Specifically, it aims to classify post-graduation employment patterns and assess demographic disparities influencing career outcomes. Design/methodology/approach Using longitudinal data covering a 36-month period after graduation, the study applies group-based multi-trajectory modeling (GBMTM) to identify distinct patterns of job status and wage progression among vocational high school graduates. Four trajectory groups are identified: long-term unemployed, gradual income entrants, early leavers, and stably employed. Multinomial regression analyses are then conducted to examine how demographic factors – including gender, region, and family background – predict membership in each trajectory group. title: Digital skills for youth employment in Africa: a systematic review
text_snippet: Digital skills for youth employment in Africa: a systematic review Purpose The purpose of this review is to quantify patterns on how digital skills relate to youth employment in Africa through a structured narrative synthesis. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA guidelines, we conducted a systematic literature review across four major databases (Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO and Dimensions). Findings All studies were in the direction of a positive relationship between digital skills and improved employment prospects for the youth. Only 10 of the 23 found significant effects. title: Sustainability-oriented teaching in vocational higher education: how intrinsic motivation, programme relevance and learning commitment shape students' social value outcomes
text_snippet: Sustainability-oriented teaching in vocational higher education: how intrinsic motivation, programme relevance and learning commitment shape students' social value outcomes Purpose This study examines whether and how sustainability-oriented teaching in vocational and applied higher education shapes students' social value-added outcomes. Drawing on self-determination theory and engagement perspectives, we test intrinsic motivation, perceived programme relevance and commitment to learning as explanatory mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of students (N = 423) in a Chinese vocational and applied higher education institution was analysed using hierarchical PLS-SEM (two-stage approach; 5,000 bootstrap resamples). title: An ecosystemic approach to sustainable graduate employability: A case study of a Sino-British joint university in China
text_snippet: An ecosystemic approach to sustainable graduate employability: A case study of a Sino-British joint university in China Purpose This article investigates the XJTLU-Academy model as an innovative case study to examine how a structured University-Industry Collaboration (UIC) mechanism cultivates learner agency and enhances graduate employability. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative single-case study design is employed, centered on the embedded XJTLU-Academy model. Findings The study identifies five interconnected operating mechanisms within the academies: curriculum co-creation, project embedding, dual mentorship, ecosystem co-creation, and collaborative evaluation. title: Liminal teacherhood: professional identity, sensemaking and employability in times of uncertainty
text_snippet: Liminal teacherhood: professional identity, sensemaking and employability in times of uncertainty Purpose This study examines how recent reforms in teacher employment in Türkiye reshape teacher candidates' professional identities and perceptions of employability. Design/methodology/approach The study uses a qualitative design based on sensemaking and liminality, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 22 third- and fourth-year teacher candidates from various public universities. Findings The analysis identifies five interrelated patterns. First, teacher identity is suspended as candidates are positioned as neither fully students nor fully teachers. Second, employability is experienced as fragile and largely externally determined, shaped by exam-centered public employment and unequal access to social and cultural resources. Third, prolonged uncertainty turns the future into an emotional burden marked by anxiety, regret and conditional attachment to the profession. Fourth, socioeconomic background strongly influences which career pathways appear open or closed, revealing employability as a socially embedded rather than individual process. title: An exploratory study of student perceptions of equity in peer assessment as part of independent group work
text_snippet: An exploratory study of student perceptions of equity in peer assessment as part of independent group work Purpose This study investigates the implementation of the peer evaluation tool “BuddyCheck” in postgraduate programmes at a UK Russell Group university, focusing on its impact on perceived equity in independent student group work. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory study using a mixed-method approach, incorporating a quantitative survey and qualitative focus groups to explore detailed perceptions of equity and the role of peer evaluation in group work. Findings “BuddyCheck” was found to enhance students' perceptions of equity in group work by providing a platform for student voice. However, its effectiveness was influenced by cultural expectations and the involvement of the lecturer/educator in the peer evaluation process. Research limitations/implications The study's findings are limited by the demographic composition of the sample, predominantly international post-graduate Chinese students. title: To bridge, link or bond: supporting the pre-graduate transitions of students from low socioeconomic backgrounds
text_snippet: To bridge, link or bond: supporting the pre-graduate transitions of students from low socioeconomic backgrounds Purpose This study examines how students from low socioeconomic backgrounds acquire social capital resources to support their transition into the graduate labour market. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods approach was employed, involving quantitative pre- and post-surveys (n = 222) and qualitative life chapter interviews (n = 25) with university students in their 3rd, 4th and 5th years. The research tested two career development interventions: a four-week bridging intervention focused on peer support around employability topics, and a linking intervention guiding students to traditional in-class career workshops. Findings Both interventions effectively reduced disparities across socioeconomic backgrounds. In addition, the study highlights the critical role of bonding social capital in the transition to employment. When students perceived a lack of bonding social capital, they faced barriers in acquiring other resources. Originality/value This research emphasises the significance of bonding social capital in employment transition interventions and demonstrates how targeted approaches can mitigate socioeconomic disparities in career development outcomes.

title: Understanding internship experiences from students’ perspectives: a systematic review
text_snippet: Understanding internship experiences from students’ perspectives: a systematic review Purpose Internships play a crucial role in shaping students’ insight into future employability. The need to gain insight into internship experiences from a student perspective related to career development is receiving increasing attention in current literature. Despite growing interest in this research topic, there is currently no clear conceptualization of internship experience. Studies remain fragmented and focus on different antecedents and outcomes of the internship experience. This makes it difficult to capture the internship experience and to understand how it fits into students’ career development. Design/methodology/approach To address this gap, a configurative systematic literature review of 204 empirical (qualitative and quantitative) articles was conducted. The review had two aims: (1) to conceptualize the internship experience, and (2), to map its antecedents and outcomes. Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT) was used as a theoretical lens to interpret the findings. title: A conceptual model for assessing student knowledge development in English lesson and learning studies
text_snippet: A conceptual model for assessing student knowledge development in English lesson and learning studies Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine how the teacher’s perceived value of student knowledge assessment (PVSKA) influences student knowledge development (SKD) in lessons and learning studies. It also explores the mediating roles of assessment approaches and methods (AAM) and assessment context (AC) in shaping this relationship. Design/methodology/approach The research is based on data collected from 558 English teachers participating in lesson and learning study projects in China. title: The role of generative artificial intelligence in enhancing creativity and its impact on university adaptation and academic performance
text_snippet: The role of generative artificial intelligence in enhancing creativity and its impact on university adaptation and academic performance Purpose This study examines how Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) relates to higher education adaptation and academic performance through creativity, using the Substitution–Augmentation–Modification–Redefinition (SAMR) model as an interpretive lens. The proposed model was examined using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). title: Developing a model for enhancing university students’ communication and collaboration skills through philosophical dialogue
text_snippet: Developing a model for enhancing university students’ communication and collaboration skills through philosophical dialogue Purpose This paper aims to develop a conceptual model for the simultaneous enhancement of communication and collaboration competencies among university students through philosophical dialogue. The study seeks to address the fragmentation in soft skills education and the lack of integrated pedagogical designs in contemporary higher education. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a qualitative, theory-building research approach. The methodology involves a systematic synthesis of academic literature, the analytical integration of the theoretical traditions of Lipman, Habermas and Freire and the abstraction of these foundations into pedagogical design principles. Findings The study proposes a dialogue-based competency development model with a three-layer structure: (1) a philosophical foundation layer, (2) a pedagogical implementation layer organized into three dialogic phases and (3) an assessment layer integrating communication, collaboration and critical thinking competencies. The model translates philosophical dialogue from an abstract principle into a pedagogical design that can be systematically organized, implemented and evaluated in higher education. Design/methodology/approach Participants expressed their attitudes towards the variables studied through a questionnaire. title: Navigating the digital divide in the Indian education system: exploring technology adoption and readiness among TVET teachers in Rajasthan
text_snippet: Navigating the digital divide in the Indian education system: exploring technology adoption and readiness among TVET teachers in Rajasthan Purpose This study investigates technology readiness and adoption among Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) teachers in Rajasthan, India, by integrating the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM 4.0) and the Technology Readiness Index (TRI). Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was conducted using multi-stage stratified random sampling across 276 TVET teachers from government and private institutions in urban and rural districts. Validated TAM and TRI scales were administered. Data were analysed using ANOVA and hierarchical multiple regression to assess structural baseline effects and the incremental explanatory contribution of acceptance beliefs and readiness dimensions. text_snippet: Cultivating an evidence-based innovation mindset in allied health professions Purpose Healthcare is a rapidly evolving field that demands allied health professionals who are both innovative and grounded in evidence-based practice. Data were analysed using inferential statistics and reflexive thematic analysis and synthesised to explore students' perceived changes in their evidence-based innovation mindset. title: Invisible but not absent: reimagining career ecosystems for NEET youth in Thailand
text_snippet: Invisible but not absent: reimagining career ecosystems for NEET youth in Thailand Purpose This study investigates how national policies, community-based initiatives, and socio-cultural dynamics interact to shape sustainable career ecosystems for NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) youth in Thailand. Addressing Sustainable Development Goal 8 on decent work and economic growth, it seeks to understand how structural, emotional, and cultural factors influence young people’s transitions from education to employment in an unequal and rapidly changing society. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative multi-site case study was conducted across three provinces, Chiang Rai, Ubon Ratchathani, and Samut Sakhon, representing diverse geographical and socio-economic contexts. The study drew on 30 semi-structured interviews and two focus group discussions with NEET youth, educators, and community stakeholders. Data were analysed thematically to identify cross-cutting patterns and contextual variations. text_snippet: The role of construction trade programs in fostering social mobility, job equity, and addressing skilled labor shortages Purpose The U.S. construction industry has faced a persistent shortage of skilled workers since the early 1980s, which poses challenges to the successful execution of construction projects. To address this shortage, this study proposes a practical workforce development solution by recruiting, educating, training, and certifying low-income individuals and members of underserved communities in construction trades. This approach promotes social mobility and job equity. Design/methodology/approach The study surveyed 114 students, alumni, and instructors from a Florida-based construction trade program (CTP) serving low-income and underserved individuals. The survey examined knowledge gaps in construction trades, whether participants found better job opportunities during or after the CTP; and which courses and instructional tools most effectively supported job placement and workforce training. text_snippet: The human impact of crisis in business schools in higher education: the role of belonging dissonance Purpose This study investigates how business school academics experienced and navigated disruptions to their sense of belonging during the COVID-19 crisis. Responding to limited research on academic belonging in times of institutional upheaval, the study develops the concept of belonging dissonance to explain the tensions created when academics' expectations of collegiality, identity affirmation and institutional support diverge from crisis-driven organisational practices. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on 153 qualitative survey responses and 12 in-depth interviews with business academics across multiple countries. title: Entrepreneurial intention in higher education during COVID-19: evidence of stability and comparability across student groups and time
text_snippet: Entrepreneurial intention in higher education during COVID-19: evidence of stability and comparability across student groups and time Purpose The main objective of this paper is to assess the measurement invariance of a short questionnaire assessing students' entrepreneurial intention (EI) over time and across key subgroups (gender, higher education institution (HEI) typology, course typology) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Design/methodology/approach A multigroup confirmatory factor analysis was conducted on data collected from undergraduate students enrolled in entrepreneurship modules at Portuguese HEIs during the second semester of the 2019/2020 academic year. Findings There is evidence of configural, metric and scalar invariance of the covariance structure of the 6-item scale of students' EI by gender, HEI typology and course typology, and over time (before and after entrepreneurship modules). In the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, these findings suggest that the 6-item scale of EI is psychometrically equivalent across key subgroups of entrepreneurship students in HEIs and over time. title: Unpacking entrepreneurial intention in adolescents: the mediating role of future vision and risk perception
text_snippet: Unpacking entrepreneurial intention in adolescents: the mediating role of future vision and risk perception Purpose The aim of this study is to examine the influence of key entrepreneurial competencies – proactivity, future vision, and risk perception – on the development of entrepreneurial intention of adolescent students in vocational education. Mediation analysis was conducted to test the hypothesized indirect effects. Findings The results revealed that proactivity does not directly predict entrepreneurial intention in adolescent students. title: The silent frontier: vocational education and its marginalization in the sociology of education
text_snippet: The silent frontier: vocational education and its marginalization in the sociology of education Purpose This conceptual paper examines why vocational education and training (VET/TVET) remains marginal within the sociology of education (SoE) despite its central role in contemporary education systems and youth transitions. It identifies epistemological, institutional and methodological blind spots and proposes a cultural–organizational framework as a conceptual language that allows the study of any kind of education by engaging with actors' meanings as well as institutional arrangements. Design/methodology/approach The paper draws on an analytical literature review and discussion of sociological, TVET and youth studies scholarship. It sides with recent suggestions made in SoE to move beyond the focus on an individual and to take institutions into account. It proposes using Amy Binder's cultural–organizational approach as a lens to reconceptualise TVET as a site of identity formation rather than merely technical skills provision. title: LinkedIn in management education: LinkedIn usage, career prospects and industry commitment
text_snippet: LinkedIn in management education: LinkedIn usage, career prospects and industry commitment Purpose LinkedIn is a prominent social media platform designed to help users connect, share, and advance their careers. This study examines the impacts of students' attitudes toward LinkedIn usage on their career interest, career prospects and industry commitment. Design/methodology/approach An online survey on the Qualtrics platform was used to recruit 93 university students of business management enrolled in classes on human resource management who were active LinkedIn users. Findings Analysis using Statistical Package for Social Sciences software indicated that students' attitudes toward LinkedIn usage and career interest were positively related to their career prospects and industry commitment. Career interest partially mediated the relationship between students' attitudes toward LinkedIn usage and their career prospects and industry commitment, respectively. Originality/value This study highlights the association between the usage of LinkedIn in higher education and students' career prospects and professional industry commitment.

title: Who are the educators participating in agricultural industry school partnerships?
text_snippet: Who are the educators participating in agricultural industry school partnerships? Purpose Little is known about the educators who participate in agricultural industry school partnerships (ISPs) and how to best support them to implement associated activities. This research explores the nature of educators who were willing to partake in agricultural ISPs by understanding what relevant experience they had, their perceptions of agriculture, and the support they need to participate. Design/methodology/approach A descriptive mixed-methods case study design was used to collect survey data from 57 educators from 2021–2023. Findings This study finds that the educators had diverse teaching experiences and connections to agriculture. Most educators had positive perceptions of the industry and career opportunities. text_snippet: Development of a human-centric pedagogical ethos for construction management education amidst industry 5.0 Purpose Pedagogical and andragogical research within higher education (HE) is ubiquitous throughout a diverse range of academic disciplines. However, pedagogical ethos with an increasingly digital curricula has attracted scant academic attention and Construction Management Education (CME) programmes are no exception. Design/methodology/approach A mixed philosophical stance of interpretivism and pragmatism is adopted together with inductive reasoning to examine construction education experts' perceptions of the phenomena investigated. title: Exploring the local enactment of internships in secondary TVET in Chile: interpretations, adjustments, barriers and enablers
text_snippet: Exploring the local enactment of internships in secondary TVET in Chile: interpretations, adjustments, barriers and enablers Purpose This study examines how secondary TVET schools in Chile implement the internship policy. Drawing on a policy enactment framework, it explores how school actors recontextualise internships to suit their local contexts, and the barriers and enablers they encounter. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a qualitative methodology, with data collected through 37 interviews with internship coordinators at secondary TVET schools across multiple cities within an administrative region in Chile. Findings The study shows that the aim of internships can be interpreted along two interrelated dimensions: instrumentality (low or high) and the focus of that instrumentality (competency validation or employability). These interpretations shape how the policy is enacted and, in turn, how students are allocated to different workplaces. It also identifies the types of barriers and enablers affecting the management and supervision of internships at the local level, including the challenges schools face in engaging with employers.
